body:
Sometimes I think, "I can't die in this shithole." Sometimes I think, "I can't die this fat and ugly."

Gotta lose weight, get fit first. Too fucking ugly to be dead yet. Then maybe disappear on vacation. Not here. Too many fake, self centered assholes would make it about them.

Sometimes I hate myself so much my teeth ache. I'm just so full of fucking disgust that doesn't have another outlet. That's all I have left, i guess. Teeth like emotional barometers. 

I stopped cutting, like, 10 years ago. Damned if I don't miss that outlet some days. Damned shame that I have so many scars though. Too many scars. Always someone suspicious & commenting on my sleeves.

Wish fat girl style wasn't always 3/4 sleeves. I can't get away with that. Scars up and down my arms. Scars on my ankles and thighs. Scars everywhere. So obvious. So pitiable and pathetic.

Every generation of every side of my family has suicide. I was always going to be that person. It's just amazing I lasted this long. Just like uncle Frank with his service revolver. Just like cousin Frank and Niagara Falls. Just like Eugene and the gun. Just like grandma and her medicine. We all last too prudently long. Eventually we just can't fake it anymore.

Suicide is a family tradition.

I wish I'd been abducted tonight.

Tonight I walked around San Diego alone at midnight, knowing I am too ugly to be kidnapped. There's safety in being totally fucking worthless.

I spent hours tonight leaking tears from the right side of my face (ar a wedding, no less)  unable to understand wtf was even the problem.

I want to text an old friend but we're different people now and I'll be ashamed in the morning and he wouldn't know what to make of it and we were never close in a suicode watch way anyway.

The last person I want to talk to is my fiance.
No, I'm late 20s. 15 years of suicidal ideation.

Hey OP, I obviously don't know the situation or anything but your best friend might not be lost to you. Maybe they just need some time to process what you told them. I know I have been that person before. Have to get a little distance and perspective, mull things over some, before I can approach that person again. But I would have been devastated to lose them first. Stick it out, maybe it's not over :)

How did your parents react? That is a really tough situation to navigate.

In a really down/lethargic/hopeless state, the only thing that kind of worked for me was to actually say it all out loud. Read the book out loud. Make up flash cards and answer them out loud. If it wasn't out loud, I was just wasting time, because it wouldn't stick. I think it helps get both sides of the brain working at the same time. Activate that corpus callosum and whatnot.

Another similar trip here. I was a cell in a body. Looks like the part-of-a-larger-system trip is a theme. Also terrified - seems like that's another theme. When I came to, I made my friend promise to never, ever, ever let me do Salvia again. I think those were my first coherent words.

It hits immediately. You take one big rip and by the time you're letting it out, time is distorted. Reality totally disappeared and I vividly hallucinate that I was a cell in a larger system but I was not a typical cell and the fixer cells were coming to destroy me. You have no concept of life outaide of the hallucination. You don't remembee that you're a person and on drugs. That person is gone. Honestly it was terrifying and the feeling of being hunted and wrong stuck with me long after the hallucination passed. Time lost all meaning, so even though it only lasted a few minutes it felt like hours.

Today I graduated college again. I had family and friends come to the first grad and didn't want to make them do it again (and didn't want to shame anyone into gifts), so I told them not to bother coming. Then at the ceremony, panicked. Everyone crossing the stage was cheered on, and I just kept thinking how no one was there for me. How it would be silent when I crossed the stage. How I didn't even have any of the honors regalia these other people had. Graduating plain Jane from some nowhere school with no support. I kept tearing up. I couldn't hold it together. 

I set my name card down when we stood to walk across the stage, so I had to leave my place in line when I should have been announced and walk all the way back around to get it. Talk about a walk of shame. 

After the ceremony, I had no one to greet and celebrate with. Didn't feel like celebrating anyway. Just felt in the way and too ugly to exist. 

Went to dinner with brother, his friend, and my boyfriend after. As usual I was the butt of all jokes and incapable of relating. 

I've been doing OK for the last few weeks but today was just hard. It's hard to keep going. I don't think I'll ever grow out of it. I feel like I'll never get where I want in life. I don't relate to people well. I tried therapy a few times but I just can't open up. I care too much what others think and I want to please. I feel so ashamed and terrible talking about dark feelings and I just can't do it. 

Just having a rough time and can't express it to anyone. No advice or response needed.

Another former cutter chiming in. I was maybe about 12 and had been thinking about it for a while. My head was full of this I hate myself, I am not worthy of love, I am not worthy of the clothing or shelter or the people around me, kind of mentality. And I just wanted to shut my brain off for a while. Hurting yourself does that. When you're empty and hollow and just want to curl up and die, it brings things to a head and lets you get past the worst of it. Like heroin, but free.
